title: Articles — Generic Reference & Common L1 Mistakes
subtitle: Know when English uses no article at all — one of the most common sources of mistakes for Portuguese speakers.
objectives: Use no article for generic plural/uncountable nouns and abstract concepts
Use no article with meals, means of transport and most institutions in fixed expressions
Recognize the specific pattern of L1 transfer from Portuguese, which usually does use an article in these cases
Contrast generic reference (no article) with a specific instance (the)

content.intro: You already know a/an/the for specific, countable, first-mention nouns. At B2, the harder skill is knowing when English uses no article at all — especially for generic statements, which is exactly where Portuguese speakers tend to add one by mistake.

rules.heading: a) Generic reference — no article
rules.body:
When you talk about something in general (not one specific example), plural and uncountable nouns take no article in English.

  • Coffee is popular in Brazil. (coffee in general — not "the coffee")
  • Dogs are loyal animals. (dogs in general — not "the dogs," unless you mean specific dogs already mentioned)
  • Compare: The coffee on the table is cold. (one specific coffee)

In Portuguese this is different: "O café é popular no Brasil" / "Os cães são leais" both use an article — English does not, for generic statements.

rules.heading: b) Abstract nouns — no article
rules.body:
Abstract concepts (love, life, happiness, freedom, information, advice, music, art) usually take no article when talking about the concept generally.

  • Life is unpredictable. (not "The life")
  • Music helps me relax. (not "The music," unless referring to specific music already mentioned)

rules.heading: c) Meals, transport and fixed expressions
rules.body:
No article in common fixed expressions:

  • Meals: have breakfast / lunch / dinner (not "the breakfast")
  • Transport: by car / by bus / by plane / on foot (not "by the car")
  • Places used for their normal purpose: go to school / go to work / go to bed / in bed / at home

content.registerNote: This is one of the most persistent errors for Portuguese speakers, since Portuguese almost always uses an article where English generic statements use none — the mistake often survives even at advanced levels, precisely because it doesn't affect comprehension, only correctness.
examples: The water in this glass is warm.
Cats sleep most of the day.
The cats next door make a lot of noise at night.
I usually have lunch at noon.
We went to Paris by train.
Children learn languages faster than adults.
He goes to bed early on weekdays.

commonMistakes.wrong: The coffee is my favorite drink.
commonMistakes.why: A generic statement about coffee in general takes no article — “the coffee” would mean one specific coffee (e.g., the one in front of you).
Abstract nouns used generically take no article.

commonMistakes.wrong: I go to the school by the bus.
commonMistakes.right: I go to school by bus.
commonMistakes.why: Institutions used for their normal purpose (school) and means of transport (by bus) take no article in these fixed expressions.
A generic statement about dogs in general — "the dogs" would only be correct if referring to specific, already-identified dogs.

commonMistakes.wrong: I like the music and the art.
commonMistakes.why: Talking about music and art as general concepts/interests, not one specific piece — no article.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Choose the, a, or (no article) for each blank.

items.prompt: ___ Books are my favorite way to relax.
items.explanation: Generic statement about books in general — no article.

items.prompt: ___ book on your desk looks interesting.
items.explanation: A specific, identifiable book ("on your desk") takes "the."
Abstract noun used generically — no article.

items.prompt: We usually have ___ dinner at eight.
items.explanation: Meals in fixed expressions take no article.

items.prompt: She travels to work by ___ bicycle.
items.explanation: Means of transport in "by + transport" takes no article.

items.prompt: ___ information you sent me was very useful.
items.explanation: This refers to specific information already mentioned/sent, not information in general.

items.incorrect: The money can't buy the happiness.
items.explanation: Both "money" and "happiness" are generic/abstract here — no article for either.

items.incorrect: I go to the bed at eleven every night.
answer: I go to bed at eleven every night.
items.explanation: "Go to bed" is a fixed expression with no article.
A generic statement about cats in general — no article.

items.incorrect: We came here by the plane.
items.explanation: "By + means of transport" is a fixed expression with no article.

exercises.title: Guided Production
exercises.instructions: Write your own sentence for each prompt. There's no single correct answer — a model answer is shown for comparison after you submit.

items.prompt: Write one generic sentence about an abstract concept (e.g., time, freedom, success) with no article.
items.modelAnswer: Success requires patience and consistent effort.

items.prompt: Write one sentence contrasting a generic plural noun (no article) with a specific instance of the same noun (with “the”).
items.modelAnswer: Books can change your perspective on life, but the books on my shelf right now are mostly unread.

summary: Generic statements about plural/uncountable nouns take no article: Coffee is popular, not The coffee is popular.
Abstract nouns used generically (life, love, happiness, music) take no article.
Fixed expressions with meals, transport and everyday institutions take no article: have breakfast, by car, go to school.
Add “the” only when referring to one specific, already-identified instance.
